message.content:
During the 19th century the sculpture that most people think of when they hear “iconic” is **Auguste Rodin’s *The Kiss*** (1889). It was one of the first modern sculptures to break away from the strict academic conventions of the time, and it quickly became a symbol of Romantic love and artistic freedom. Its dramatic pose, expressive surface treatment, and the way it captures a fleeting moment of intimacy made it instantly recognizable and widely reproduced.

Other works that were hugely influential in the same period include:

| Sculpture | Artist | Year | Why it mattered |
|-----------|--------|------|-----------------|
| *The Gates of Hell* | Rodin | 1880‑1917 (unfinished) | A monumental, complex work that pushed the limits of scale and emotional intensity. |
| *The Thinker* | Rodin | 1902‑03 (first cast) | Though its first casts appeared just after the century ended, the design was conceived in the 1890s and it became a universal icon of contemplation. |
| *Laocoön* (recast) | Various | 1885 | A faithful recreation of the ancient marble that revived interest in classical forms. |

So if you’re looking for the single sculpture that captured the public imagination across Europe and America in the 1800s, *The Kiss* is usually the answer.
